title: Injection / Input Validation
summary: Untrusted input flows into a query, command, path, or template without being separated from the instruction. A crafted value then changes what the code executes. The fix is almost always to pass the value as data (a bound parameter, an argv list, a safe join) rather than concatenating it into a string.
example_bad:
q = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '{email}'"
db.execute(q)

title: Auth & Access Control
summary: The code authenticates a user but never checks that this user is allowed to touch this resource. Any logged-in caller can act on another user's data by changing an id (IDOR), or a role check is written so it always passes. The fix is an explicit ownership or permission check against the current user before the action.

title: Error & Exception Handling
summary: A failure is swallowed instead of handled. A bare except that does nothing, a return value that is never checked, or an error path that leaves the object half-built. The caller then proceeds on bad data and fails later with a confusing message. The fix is to catch the specific error, act on it, and signal failure clearly.

title: Concurrency & State
summary: Two things run at once and step on shared state. A check-then-act gap where another thread slips in between, a counter updated without a lock, or a default argument shared across calls. The bug is timing-dependent and hard to reproduce. The fix is to make the read-modify-write atomic, or to not share the state at all.
example_bad:
if key not in cache:
    cache[key] = factory()

title: Logic & Boundary
summary: The code runs but computes the wrong thing. An off-by-one in a loop bound, a comparison that should be >= not >, a condition that is inverted, or the wrong branch returned. No crash, just quietly wrong output. The fix is to trace the boundary and edge cases by hand.
example_bad:
for i in range(len(arr)):
    if arr[i] == arr[i + 1]:  # IndexError on the last i
example_good:
for i in range(len(arr) - 1):
    if arr[i] == arr[i + 1]:

title: Resource & Performance
summary: The code holds a resource it never releases, or does work that grows faster than the input. A connection opened per loop and never closed, a cache that grows forever, or an O(n) membership test inside an O(n) loop. It works on small inputs and falls over on real ones. The fix is a context manager, a bound, or a better data structure.
